hypothesis: A testable prediction or explanation based on observations. A good hypothesis can be proven wrong by an experiment.
experiment: A controlled procedure designed to test a hypothesis. Good experiments change only one variable at a time.
variable: Any factor that can change in an experiment. The independent variable is what you change; the dependent variable is what you measure.
control group: The group in an experiment that does not receive the experimental treatment. Used as a baseline to compare results.
peer review: The process where other scientists evaluate a study before it is published. Helps catch errors and ensures quality.
theory: In science, a well-tested, well-supported explanation for a broad set of observations. Much stronger than everyday use of the word 'theory.'
law: A description of a consistent pattern in nature. Scientific laws describe what happens; theories explain why.
atom: The smallest unit of a chemical element that retains the properties of that element. Made of protons, neutrons, and electrons.
molecule: Two or more atoms bonded together. Water (H₂O) is two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom.
force: A push or pull acting on an object. Forces change the motion of objects. Measured in Newtons.
mass: The amount of matter in an object. Different from weight — mass stays the same regardless of gravity.
weight: The gravitational force acting on an object's mass. Weight = mass × gravitational acceleration.
velocity: The speed of an object in a specific direction. Speed tells you how fast; velocity tells you how fast AND which way.
acceleration: The rate of change of velocity. An object accelerates when it speeds up, slows down, or changes direction.
energy: The ability to do work or cause change. Energy cannot be created or destroyed — only converted from one form to another.
kinetic energy: The energy an object has because of its motion. A moving car has kinetic energy. The faster it moves and the more mass it has, the more kinetic energy.
potential energy: Stored energy based on position or condition. A boulder at the top of a hill has gravitational potential energy.
DNA: Deoxyribonucleic acid. The molecule that carries genetic information in living organisms. Shaped like a double helix.
cell: The basic unit of life. All living things are made of cells. Some organisms are one cell; the human body contains about 37 trillion.
evolution: The process by which species change over generations through natural selection. Organisms that are better adapted to their environment survive and reproduce more.
natural selection: The mechanism of evolution. Organisms with traits that help them survive and reproduce pass those traits to their offspring.
photosynthesis: The process by which plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce glucose (food) and oxygen.
